proves.claim: every seats test file that reads files carries an input header naming the cells it reads.

seats.inputs.readers-declare.why: A reader with no header hides what its result depends on.

proves.claim: with the declared-inputs rule on no seats reader is reported, and a header names a cell, never the whole tree.

seats.inputs.no-whole-tree.why: A whole-tree header would make every change rerun the test.

proves.claim: the project registry uses validated repo labels, refreshes metadata, prunes missing roots and forgets one path.

seats.registry.metadata-refresh-prune-fo.why: A registry that kept stale roots or wrote invalid labels misled the person inventory.

proves.claim: parallel processes preserve 30 registrations across a killed lock owner.

seats.registry.parallel-30-killed-owner.why: A killed lock owner once lost registrations made by parallel processes.

proves.claim: a project whose tiers name only self-hosted endpoints routes a routine item to the routine tier and an escalation item to the escalation tier.

seats.tier.self-hosted-routing.why: Self-hosted-only tiers routed every item to one tier.

proves.claim: same-session writes in one checkout run side by side while a takeover still waits for them.

seats.checkout.same-session-writes.why: A takeover that did not wait corrupted writes made in the same session.

proves.claim: temporary roots and symlinked previews stay out of the person inventory.

seats.projects.temp-roots-excluded.why: Temporary boards cluttered the person inventory.

proves.claim: agent scratch and explicit transient previews are excluded without hiding ordinary agent projects.

seats.projects.agent-scratch-excluded.why: Hiding ordinary agent projects lost real boards from the inventory.

proves.claim: a normal repository remains listed and a custom registry does not admit temporary boards.

seats.projects.normal-repo-listed.why: A custom registry let temporary boards back in.

proves.claim: the shipped profiles load, giving a known runtime its cache setting and an unknown one a safe default.

seats.runtime-profile.shipped-profiles-l.why: An unknown runtime without a safe default broke seat setup.

proves.claim: a live seat with no commit, submit or gate for 30 minutes gets exactly one nudge.

seats.watchdog.one-nudge-after-30-min.why: Repeated nudges spammed a seat that was already warned.

proves.claim: a seat that is not otherwise live is not nudged.

seats.watchdog.not-live-not-nudged.why: Nudging a dead seat wasted attention and created noise.

proves.claim: a flagged claim with no progress 10 minutes after the nudge is released back to next.

seats.watchdog.flagged-claim-released.why: A silent claim blocked its item indefinitely.

proves.claim: progress after the nudge clears the flag, and a submit or gate in the last 10 minutes is never touched.

seats.watchdog.progress-clears-flag.why: A seat making progress lost its claim.

proves.claim: itemTierPin returns the tier named by the last tier-pin note, and null when there is none.

seats.tier-pin.last-note-wins.why: A wrong pin sent an item to the wrong tier.

proves.claim: a later tier-pin replaces an earlier pin and an empty tier-pin clears it.

seats.tier-pin.replace-and-clear.why: A pin that could not be replaced or cleared trapped an item on one tier.

proves.claim: bouncesAtTier counts the rejects and returned reviews routed at the tier.

seats.tier-bounces.count-at-tier.why: A wrong bounce count escalated items too early or too late.

proves.claim: the bounce count restarts when the tier pin changes.

seats.tier-bounces.restart-on-pin-change.why: Old bounces counted against a tier the item had left.

proves.claim: the longest owned prefix decides a path's lane; unowned paths are the coordinator's.

seats.lanes.longest-prefix-decides.why: A shorter prefix matching first gave a path to the wrong lane.

proves.claim: a lane may change its own paths and shared ones; the coordinator may change anything.

seats.lanes.who-may-change.why: A lane changing another lane's paths broke lane ownership.

proves.claim: lane names list the coordinator first.

seats.lanes.coordinator-first.why: A reordered lane list moved the coordinator out of first place.

proves.claim: a config with a bad lane refuses and names the field.

seats.lanes.bad-lane-refuses.why: A bad lane loaded silently and failed later.

proves.claim: config merges nested groups over the defaults, and leases read as durations.

seats.lanes.config-merge-leases.why: A shallow merge dropped default settings inside a group.

proves.claim: the review queue ratio is configurable and invalid values name their field.

seats.lanes.review-ratio-configurable.why: An invalid ratio was accepted without naming the field.

proves.claim: a claim's lease is 2h unless pullboard.json says otherwise.

seats.lanes.claim-lease-default.why: A wrong default lease expired claims early.

proves.claim: lightShaped is true for one clause, one test file and at most two brief files, and false when any limit is exceeded.

seats.route.light-shaped-limits.why: A wrong light shape routed heavy items to light seats.

proves.claim: settings line given level.liveOnly or route.liveOnly orders setLineSetting with the stored key route.liveOnly.

seats.logic-line-settings-cli.level-name.why: The rename is input-side only; a changed stored key would break the engine floor and every replayed event.

proves.claim: the settings line list and the confirmation print level.liveOnly for the stored route.liveOnly.

seats.logic-line-settings-cli.list-shows.why: The person types and reads one name; showing the stored key would keep the old name alive.

proves.claim: every seats-cell test has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

seats.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.
